Subject: Request: 2-week extension + discount for pilot

Hi Ben,

We ran into an internal procurement delay and will not be able to finish the pilot evaluation by the original end date (Jan 20). The product team still wants to validate a couple of performance scenarios (KV cache behavior with our long-context prompts), but legal/procurement need additional time to process the SOW.

Two asks from our side: would Redwood consider either (A) a 2-week extension to the pilot with no change to pricing, or (B) a one-time credit to offset overage if we need to run extra tests? If you can do a small discount/credit, it would help get procurement over the line.

We'd also appreciate a short note that any evaluation data will be retained for only 30 days post-pilot for compliance reasons.

Thanks — appreciate the help.

Best,
Aisha
Senior Product Manager
Brightline Health

Hi Aisha — thanks for the note and for flagging the procurement timing. Sorry to hear about the delay. We can support you here; two quick options below and a preferred recommendation from my side: 

Option A — Time extension only
- Add two calendar weeks to the existing pilot end date (no financial change).
- We keep the same usage caps; any overage billed per our pilot rate.

Option B — One-time evaluation credit (preferred)
- Redwood issues a one-time credit tied to the pilot equal to $4,000 to cover additional test runs (applies to token usage only).
- Credit expires 30 days after the new pilot end date.

If compliance needs the retention statement, we can confirm in the addendum that evaluation logs are retained for 30 days post-pilot and then deleted. Laura (cc'd) can add the clause.

Quick question: what success criteria do you want to use to decide conversion? If we can align on 2–3 metrics (latency P50/P95, accuracy on the sample prompt set, and cost per inference), we can extend the SOW to include them and speed approvals.

I attached a short addendum that reflects Option B language and the 30-day retention note — take a look and send any redlines. If procurement requires a discount instead of credit, tell me the number and I can escalate.

Thanks,
Ben
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0142

Subject: FW: Request: 2-week extension + discount for pilot — recs

Team — forwarding Brightline's ask. Procurement wants either a short pricing concession or more runway. My recommendation: offer Option B (one-time credit) at $4k and a 2-week extension contingent on signing the attached addendum. Rationale: preserves list price, reduces conversion friction, limited window to avoid precedent.

Laura: can you draft the retention language (30 days) and a one-line clause that the credit is non-recurring and applies only to this pilot?
Grace: if we accept the credit, let's also document the success metrics (latency P95 < 600ms on their sample set, accuracy threshold 0.78 on labeled prompts) so we can objectively evaluate. If they can't meet either, CS will run a focused troubleshooting session.

I'll propose the DocuSign flow to procurement once we have legal text.

-Ben
